_fields.key: stable ASCII slug — never change once published
_fields.name_ru: canonical Russian ingredient name, noun-first. This is the ONLY spelling that should appear in recipes[].ingredients[].name
_fields.cat: shopping-list category heading (Russian). Fixes the 27-heading drift across W22-W26.
_fields.tags: classification used by validate-plan.js: protein categories, legume/soy/oat markers, ldl_nut, etc.
_fields.species: for fish only — drives the 'different species each time' variety rule
_fields.basis: 'dry' means per100g refers to uncooked weight (grains, legumes, pasta). Recipes must state dry weight for these.
_fields.per100g: kcal, p=protein_g, c=carbs_g, f=fat_g, sf=sat_fat_g, fib=fiber_g, na=sodium_mg, ca=calcium_mg, fe=iron_mg, zn=zinc_mg. Optional, default 0: fs=free_sugars_g (WHO definition — added sugars plus those in honey/syrups/juice; NOT sugar in intact fruit or milk), st=plant_sterols_stanols_g, vf=viscous_soluble_fiber_g (beta-glucan, pectin, mucilage — the LDL-active fraction, not total soluble fibre).
_fields._micronutrient_caveat: ca/fe/zn are TOTAL intake from standard composition tables, not bioavailable intake. A large share of the iron and calcium in a spice- and wholegrain-heavy menu is poorly absorbed, and phytate in legumes/grains further reduces it. Budgets keyed to these values are warn-level in targets.json for that reason — treat them as a floor-detector, not a measurement. vf values are the least certain of all: beta-glucan in oats/barley is well characterised, the pectin and mucilage figures are approximations.
_fields.g_per: unit → grams conversion for non-gram units (pcs, slice, cloves, stalks, tsp)
_fields.density: grams per ml, for ingredients measured in ml. Default 1.0.
_fields.aliases: every historical spelling seen in data/weeks/*.json, so old files still resolve

_note: Unknown ingredient names are a hard failure in scripts/compute-nutrition.js. To introduce a new food, add an entry here. That keeps ingredient naming canonical forever and makes shopping categories stable.
